recommendations.rationale: The executed single-state, single-horizon probe shows the recorded command is not the maximal braking at update 33 (endpoint tip speed 0.6851514257340946 m/s versus 0.5827480226234343 m/s for the instantaneous braking box), yet even the braking box ends far above the 0.02 m/s settling limit after 0.01 s; the result therefore neither supports nor excludes objective weighting, solver stop-short, effective horizon or projected-model causes, and no further check is authorized. Deferring the recommendation executes nothing by itself, and any control-parameter change would be unsupported by this evidence.

attribution.reason: At the update-33 projected state the recorded applied tension leaves a 0.01 s endpoint tip speed above the instantaneous braking-box endpoint (0.6851514257340946 vs 0.5827480226234343 m/s) and applies less speed reduction (-0.7719393694366347 vs -0.874342772547295 m/s), so the recorded command is not the maximal braking available at that state. The gap is modest relative to the endpoint speeds themselves, and even the braking-box input still ends far above the 0.02 m/s limit after 0.01 s, so this supports a local under-braking observation only; it does not by itself explain the residual late tip speed or the closed-loop settling failure.

Terminal (0.6351726092425104 m/s) and late-window max (1.5810152739742807 m/s) tip speeds greatly exceed the 0.02 m/s settling limit while terminal position is within tolerance, and the retained recipe records small velocity/tip-speed weights. Raw weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance, and no per-term cost contributions or iteration traces are retained, so the executed local probe cannot test whether these weights let residual tip speed be accepted.

34 of 35 selections are 'User_Requested_Stop' against 1 'Solve_Succeeded', with plans nonetheless accepted; the counts show stops short of a convergence criterion but do not establish suboptimality or its link to settling, and the single-state probe did not vary solver behaviour. No iteration traces are retained to test this.

Effective horizon declines from 8 to 3 control intervals across the sampled late updates (configured horizon 10); reduced lookahead could limit braking/terminal-speed shaping, but the retained signals do not separate horizon from solver stops, objective weighting, or the local command, and the probe used a fixed 0.01 s horizon.

Projected-GVS predictions and recorded serial-backend endpoints differ by small nonzero world-tip distances and one-step velocity norms, and the executed comparison is itself a projected-model probe from a projected state; a single boxed 0.01 s comparison cannot establish that this mismatch dominates settling or separate it from a command-braking effect.

35 deadline misses and mean_update_s 17.075238151415917 s against a 0.01 s control period are recorded, but the schedule is synchronous with fixed backend steps and controller calls completing before them, so wall-clock deadline misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time and cannot directly cause the physical settling failure.

Applied tension reaches 7.990411884680996 N on near_t0 at update 30 near the 8 N per-channel limit, and the braking-box row of the executed comparison drives the tension box hard (two channels at the 8 N limit) while both rows still report input_bounds_satisfied true; the check does not quantify braking authority lost to the per-channel limit, so force-limit proximity remains unresolved.

facts.statement: Reach passed while sampled settling failed: terminal tip error 0.007642608585867386 m is within the 0.01 m reach tolerance and reach_passed is true, but sampled_settling_passed is false with late-window max tip error 0.05813810428573256 m against the 0.01 m settling position limit.
Tip speed is far above the settling limit: terminal tip speed 0.6351726092425104 m/s and late-window max tip speed 1.5810152739742807 m/s both exceed the 0.02 m/s settling_criteria speed limit.

Retained configuration records velocity_weight 0.0001, terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0, holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0, terminal_weight 5.0 and tracking_weight 1.0; no per-objective-term cost contributions or optimizer iteration traces are retained.

Executed single-state check (model.gvs@1.0.0, implicit Euler, horizon 0.01 s, step 0.002 s) at the saved projected state of update 33 (t=0.33 s; start tip speed 1.4570907951707293 m/s): the recorded applied tension ends at endpoint tip speed 0.6851514257340946 m/s, whereas the instantaneous braking-box input ends at 0.5827480226234343 m/s; both endpoints remain far above the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit.

Over that fixed 0.01 s horizon the recorded-input row (holding the update-33 applied tension vector [5.661220351760543, 3.988726293001102, 5.0287952725384195e-05, 1.4347363175658354, 1.0812420082241823, 0.003992529299500661] N) reduces tip speed by 0.7719393694366347 m/s versus 0.874342772547295 m/s for the braking-box row, and both rows report input_bounds_satisfied true.

At the same check the recorded-input endpoint tip error is 0.009842592258858245 m at tip position [0.2811575960633344, 0.035432429209937166, 0.19430133932320742] m (within the 0.01 m settling position limit), while the braking-box endpoint displacement is 0.005559344630308817 m; the endpoint position difference between the two inputs is small on the scale of the 0.01 m limit.

The executed comparison is advisory-only, single-state and single-horizon: advisory_only is true, horizon_s 0.01, integration_step_s 0.002, at the saved projected state t=0.33 s of controller update 33; it is a local projected-model endpoint probe and not a closed-loop settling result.

Late-window selections ended short of convergence with shrinking lookahead: effective horizon falls from 8 control intervals at update 27 to 3 at update 32, only 1 of 35 selections reports 'Solve_Succeeded' versus 34 'User_Requested_Stop', and the run logs 35 deadline misses with mean_update_s 17.075238151415917 s against a 0.01 s control period.

Matched projected-GVS versus recorded-backend comparisons at the late updates show small but nonzero world-tip differences (0.0059230819406683064 m at update 27) and one-step velocity-vector difference norms of 0.021386880777076088 m/s (update 28) and 0.14969247760063253 m/s (update 29).
Applied tension on the near_t0 channel reaches 7.990411884680996 N at update 30, close to the 8 N per-channel limit retained in source.force_limits for all six tendons.

limitations: The single authorized 0.01 s saved-state check has been spent at one saved projected state (update 33, t=0.33 s) under model.gvs@1.0.0, implicit Euler, step 0.002 s; no further check is authorized, and a single-state, single-horizon probe cannot establish closed-loop settling behaviour or a dominant cause.

Model limit: the comparison uses the projected GVS model, not the serial backend, so projected-versus-backend mismatch (small nonzero matched tip and velocity differences at updates 27-29) cannot be separated from command effects at this state.

Projected-state limit: the probe starts from the projected measured_initial_state of update 33, which is a projected GVS state, not the full backend state; per-update saved projected states other than update 33 were not read in this context.

Input limit: both rollouts hold their input fixed and the braking box is an instantaneous affine-input construction on the unilateral tension box; neither represents a held-input or closed-loop braking strategy.

Integration and horizon limit: horizon_s 0.01 with integration_step_s 0.002 gives five implicit-Euler steps, so the endpoint speeds (0.6851514257340946 and 0.5827480226234343 m/s) are local observations that need not persist, and even the braking box leaves the endpoint far above the 0.02 m/s limit.

No per-objective-term cost contributions or optimizer iteration traces are retained (source.historical_full_plans not retained), so weighting, seed selection and stop-short mechanisms remain unmeasured; raw weight magnitudes alone cannot establish cost importance.

Wall-clock deadline misses and mean update wall time are recorded but, under synchronous fixed-step scheduling, do not inject physical delay into simulated time and are not evidence of a physical feedback delay.

Full sampled backend q/qdot are retained in source.backend_motion, but the motion view displayed only the final settling window (0.30-0.35 s) and no closed-loop counterfactual replay capability exists.
recommended_actions: Do not adopt a control-parameter change on this evidence: the executed check shows a modest local under-braking at one late state while weighting, solver stop-short, horizon and projected-model mismatch stay unresolved, and no further check is authorized.

If further evidence is later authorized, the discriminating directions would be per-objective-term cost contributions, closed-loop counterfactual replay, and braking-authority measurement against the 8 N per-channel limit; none of these capabilities is available in the retained inventory.
